#1289. 18 Most Decorated Players in Football History Ranked by Trophies Won

Every football player dreams of lifting as much silverware as they can possibly get their hands on. However, some of the best players to have played the beautiful game have curiously bare-looking trophy cabinets, proving how difficult it is to win any honour in the sport.

Players such as Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have made it look easy for many years, as the duo have led their respective teams to an unbelievable number of trophies over their long and storied careers for club and country.

Then there are players like Zlatan Ibrahimovic who, while also brilliant footballers in their own right, move around the most historically successful clubs in the world to chase silverware at will.

We've listed the most successful players in football history, based on the number of trophies they have amassed throughout their playing careers.

There's even a chance for a couple of these players to add further to their already sensational hauls.

A man who doesn't need any introduction at all. Zlatan Ibrahimovic was a serial winner wherever he went during his journeyman football career. He won trophies in five different countries: in the Netherlands with Ajax, in Italy with Inter Milan and AC Milan, in Spain with Barcelona, in France with Paris Saint-Germain, and in England with Manchester United.

The Swedish maverick won almost every trophy there was to win during his time as a footballer, apart from the ever-elusive Champions League. He would be further up this list had Juventus' Serie A titles in 2004/05 and 2005/06 not been revoked. There will be no more opportunities to add further silverware for the Swede, as he announced his retirement in 2023. A sad day for the sport, though he continues to be in and around the game as one of 10 legendary ex-footballers who now own a club.

5x (2006–07, 2007–08, 2008–09, 2010–11, 2021–22)

From England's Manchester United to Italian giants AC Milan, ChatGPT has ranked the biggest clubs in world football - in order.

A tremendous footballer, Xavi was a key cog for a Barcelona side that dominated football at the back end of the 2000s and the first half of the 2010s. He won 25 trophies during his illustrious 17-year stint in Barcelona's first team, including four Champions League titles, with his tiki-taka brilliance alongside Andres Iniesta not going unnoticed.

He also guided Spain to success in back-to-back European Championships (2008 and 2012) as well as the 2010 World Cup. Xavi became a manager after hanging up his boots and led Barcelona to a La Liga title from the dugout rather than in the middle of the park, before being replaced by Hansi Flick. In his twilight years, he moved to Al Saad in Qatar and added four more trophies to his tally, and has recently taken on a new role in international football as the Netherlands' helmsman.

8x (1998–99, 2004–05, 2005–06, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2012–13, 2014–15)

Winning trophies isn’t for everyone, but to do it with such poise and know-how as Luka Modric has done over the years is commendable. Between 2005/06 and 2007/08, the Croat won everything there was to win domestically with Dinamo Zagreb before enduring a trophy-less four-year stint with Tottenham Hotspur.

A move to Real Madrid beckoned - and the rest is history, as they say. Having picked up a handful of trophies since arriving in 2012, the one-time Ballon d’Or winner has won the Champions League six times, La Liga on four occasions and is a five-time Spanish Super Cup winner. Poised to collect more before hanging up his boots, the 41-year-old is a bona fide winner – and will hope to lift more silverware now at AC Milan.

5x (2012–13, 2017–18, 2019–20, 2021–22, 2023–24)

5x (2014–15, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2022–23, 2024-25)

6x (2013–14, 2015–16, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2021–22, 2023–24)

A cool and collected figure in the Real Madrid engine room, Toni Kroos waltzed himself onto the list with 34 trophies to boot. Impressively, six of those are Champions Leagues - five of which have been secured in Spain. Even while at Bayern Munich, the midfielder was somewhat of a serial winner.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Toni Kroos is one of five players to have won six Champions League titles, joining Luka Modric, Nacho Fernandez, Dani Carvajal and Paco Gento.

He collected three Bundesliga titles in six years, alongside a UEFA Super Cup and three German Cups. Unlike many players on this list, Griefswald-born Kroos is also a World Cup winner with Germany. Fittingly, in his final game for Los Blancos, the German midfielder won yet another Champions League title. What a fantastic player.

5x (2013–14, 2014–15, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2022–23)

6x (2012–13, 2015–16, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2021–22, 2023–24)

The 10 footballers who have claimed the most individual awards during their illustrious careers

Maxwell’s legacy is a curious one. That he has won 35 titles in his career is fascinating. That he barely registers as one of football’s all-time greats is even more so. But perhaps that's down to the fact the clubs he played for often flattered him, with stints at Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona, Inter Milan, and Ajax seeing him stay in cruise control while mopping up almost every honour available to him.

With just 10 Brazil caps to his name, he was never the star of any show. But with a remarkable 11 league titles and a Champions League to his name, the retired left-back probably won't care that much.

Mr. Bayern Munich himself, Thomas Muller made 756 appearances for Die Roten, scoring 250 goals, providing 285 assists, and playing a pivotal role in 13 Bundesliga titles and two Champions League triumphs. He also ranks among the top for most assists in World Cup history, having helped Germany secure the 2014 World Cup.

What's more, the understated workhorse is in the top 20 all-time Champions League goal scorers, while he also has the same number of assists in Europe’s leading club competition as Xavi. Taking those goals and assists into consideration, Muller is definitely one of the most underrated players in football history. But what he lacks in individual accolades, he most certainly makes up for in team honours. Indeed, Muller won his 35th title in October 2025, as he helped new club Vancouver Whitecaps to the Canadian Championship.

13x (2009-10, 2010-11, 2011-12, 2012-13, 2014-15, 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23, 2024-25)

8x (2010–11, 2012–13, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2018-19, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23)

6x (2009–10, 2012–13, 2013–14, 2015-16, 2018-19, 2019-20)

Ryan Giggs' longevity was something else, and it will perhaps never be seen again in the rough and tuble of English football. The Welshman started off as a tricky winger with electric pace and then transitioned into a playmaker in his latter years, allowing him to play a key role for Manchester United until he hung up his boots at the age of 40.

Giggs spent his whole 24-year professional career at the Red Devils, where he won 35 trophies. His 13 Premier League titles is a record that may never be beaten. A large part of the winger's success at Old Trafford came through the trust shown in him by Sir Alex Ferguson for so many years. That faith certainly paid off, and he was a key figure under the guise of his manager's reign of terror.

13x (1992–93, 1993–94, 1995–96, 1996–97, 1998–99, 1999–2000, 2000–01, 2002–03, 2006–07, 2007–08, 2008–09, 2010–11, 2012–13)

9x (1993, 1994, 1996, 1997, 2003, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2013)

'King Kenny' established himself as a Celtic and Liverpool legend during his career as a professional footballer. After winning 11 trophies in Scotland, Kenny Dalglish moved to Liverpool where he won everything there was to win, including six First Division titles and three European Cup trophies.

Modern fans may know him better as the man who guided Blackburn Rovers to the Premier League title in 1994/95, but Dalglish was a serial winner during his playing days. To this day, he is regarded as one of Liverpool's greatest-ever players, which is quite a compliment with the wealth of talent to have performed and lifted trophies in front of the Anfield faithful, and he also became a pretty successful manager after that as well, winning a further four league titles (though they are not counted in the glorious table below).

6x (1978–79, 1979–80, 1981–82, 1982–83, 1983–84, 1985–86)

When you think of the greatest midfielders in the past 30 years, Andres Iniesta is a name that immediately springs to mind. The midfield maestro won everything there was to win during a 16-year spell in Barcelona's first-team, including nine La Liga titles and four Champions Leagues. His greatest moment came in the 2010 World Cup final when he scored a dramatic 116th-minute winner for Spain against the Netherlands.

Iniesta announced his retirement in October 2024, describing his decision as "the most difficult of my life". What's next for him remains to be seen, but it's possible that we'll see him involved in coaching in some capacity in the near future, like many of his Catalan teammates.

9x (2004–05, 2005–06, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2012–13, 2014–15, 2015–16, 2017–18)

6x (2008–09, 2011–12, 2014–15, 2015–16, 2016–17, 2017–18)

Cristiano Ronaldo moved further up the list after securing his second UEFA Nations League title with Portugal. The Al-Nassr forward scored Portugal's all-important equaliser against Spain before being substituted through injury. However, his teammates won the penalty shootout, and helped to deliver Ronaldo his third piece of international silverware.

The five-time Champions League winner has an incredible appetite to succeed and that has not waned despite now being 41 years old. The Portuguese footballer is still going strong despite his advancing years, and you wouldn't bet against him moving even further up this list at some point in the next couple of seasons as his longevity continues to shock the world, even after having decided to hang up hbis boots for the final time with Portugal.

5x (2007–08, 2013–14, 2015–16, 2016–17, 2017–18)

#1288. UECL | Atalanta 1-1 Kairat Almaty: Dea crisis drags on with meagre point

The Atalanta wait for a victory drags on to seven matches, as they scraped a 1-1 draw with Kairat Almaty in the Conference League thanks to Nikola Krstovic.

La Dea were in crisis after scraping two draws from six competitive games, culminating in a humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Parma on Monday, so went into a three-day training retreat to prepare for this match. Thomas Kristensen, Gianluca Gaetano, Raoul Bellanova, Franck Kessie, Sead Kolasinac, Isak Hien, Giacomo Raspadori and Odilon Kossounou were injured, so youth team defender Javison Idele made his first start. They beat Pafos 3-1, but then lost 2-0 away to Ajax in this tournament.

Kairat Almaty dropped out of the Champions League and Europa League preliminary rounds after winning the Kazakhstan title, drawing at Riga and losing 5-1 to Panathinaikos in the Conference League.  Striker Jorginho had been out since July with a torn ACL, but this was only their second game under caretaker manager Zhora Arutyunyan.

Jonathan Rowe stung the goalkeeper’s gloves from the edge of the area, then nodded over as the move continued.

Kairat almost scored a comical own goal when Damir Kassabulat didn’t look at his goalkeeper for a back pass, dribbling it wide of an open goal after 11 minutes.

A ferocious Rowe strike from outside the box was acrobatically palmed out from under the bar, while Marco Carnesecchi needed a double save on Alexandr Mrynskiy and the Gustavo Mendonca follow-up.

Atalanta should’ve taken the lead on the half-hour with a well-worked passing move, but Mario Pasalic only grazed the outside of the near post from close range.

La Dea were caught out on a classic counter-attack with an Edmilson pass from the centre-circle to send Marc Gual running against two defenders, beating the on-rushing Carnesecchi.

Idele couldn’t keep the volley down from seven yards on the Nicola Zalewski cross, while when Eljif Elmas did have the ball in the net on 65 minutes, he was offside to redirect the wayward Zalewski strike.

Elmas put real power behind his curling attempt from the edge of the box, forcing a flying save from the Kairat Almaty goalkeeper.

There was another tough save on the Ederson half-volley from close range and Atalanta equalised on the resulting flapped corner, as it was knocked back from the by-line by Relja Obric for Nikola Krstovic to bundle over the line from six yards.

Atalanta pushed to the bitter end and had a huge chance to win it in stoppages, but Mario Pasalic couldn’t keep the finish on target.

Scraped? Atalanta played better and managed to come back from going behind after being hit on the break, yet again. The stats show a different story.

#1287. Allan Saint-Maximin Leads Very Different Life Away From Football

In England, Premier League fans will best remember Allan Saint-Maximin for his time at Newcastle United between 2019 and 2023. These days, the French winger plays for MLS club Charlotte FC, but – away from football – he has a very different life going on at the same time.

Saint-Maximin scored 13 goals and claimed 21 assists in 124 games for Newcastle. More than his stats, though, the winger caught the eye with his electric style of play. This helped him earn a £23m move Al-Ahli in 2023, but he's career since then has been that of a journeyman.

He was loaned out to Turkish side Fenerbahce after just one season in Saudi, and then joined Club América in Mexico one summer later. By February, he was sold to Lens, but only months later joined Charlotte in the United States.

With two goals and four assists in his first 15 games for the MLS club, he's settling in steadily enough, but the 29-year-old had reasons away from football to be content with his prospects right now anyway.

The 28-year-old has issued a statement following his sudden exit on Saturday.

As revealed in an interview with The Athletic, Saint-Maximin recently had the chance to make millions from his venture outside of football. The business in question is known as Helios, which is a Greek mythology-inspired card game created by the former Newcastle man.

The MLS star has claimed that he received a £22m (€26m) offer for the business, but turned it down as he wants to continue growing his free-to-play game. He explained:

“The journey is not about money. It’s to create something, to create jobs for people, to create opportunities.”

Saint-Maximin added that, despite rejecting the offer, he would prefer to bring in others to work alongside him, each taking a stake in the company in return for their investment.

It's not the first time he's spoken about Helios, named after the sun god. In 2022, he explained how he grew up with an interest in Greek mythology. This inspired him to combine his love for board games with the topic and create the game. He would even take it on team buses when travelling to away games.

"When I was young, I learned about Zeus and Athena and saw a lot of films and anime movies with them in," he said. "When you start to understand it, you really love it.”

According to Helios' official rulebook, the aim of the game is to win by earning coins or stealing them from your opponent. Saint-Maximin explained how he developed it, adding: “There was a lot of work, a lot of nights, because you need to come up with a new idea.

"I tested it with friends. We started to play small tournaments at home. It took two and a half years — but I am really happy that I didn’t stop.”

These days, his company appears to be going from strength to strength, and could even one day put him among footballers who have become successful businessmen

#1286. 'It's not a concern': Why Enzo Maresca will stick with 'awe-inspiring' Gianluigi Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show, growing catalogue of errors and a worrying downward trend

Published: 12:00 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:00 EDT, 5 November 2026

There was a Manchester City fan on Thursday’s Ryanair flight back home from Leipzig wearing a Gianluigi Donnarumma sticker on his coat, portraying the Italian as Don Vito Corleone. The sticker, a bit worn and a bit crumpled, was peeling off. A metaphor exists within that somewhere.

Tough times for Donnarumma, a calamitous night in the Champions League – beaten at his near post by Ridle Baku's cross for one goal, fumbling another routine effort at the feet of a striker and allowing a straightforward shot to squirm through his fingers – just adding to the feeling that the past few weeks have not reflected kindly on him.

Question marks around Donnarumma’s suitability between the sticks are becoming more pronounced after a catalogue of mistakes this season. One against Paris Saint-Germain when Maghnes Akliouche’s shot was too hot (some would argue two after neglecting his near post for Desire Doue’s opener) and then Nicolas Jackson shooting through him at Aston Villa last month.

Each time, Enzo Maresca has publicly recognised the errors and intimated that nobody needs to rake over them in detail with his No1, who is experienced enough to know he must do better.

Now Leipzig. ‘It’s not a concern,’ Maresca said of the latest gaffe. The manager’s defences of Donnarumma are racking up and what City are witnessing is fundamental problems from somebody described as the best the world has to offer.

Maresca has rejected the idea that summer signing Geronimo Rulli, a 34-year-old Argentina international, could take over the gloves, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’. Rulli understood his lot when joining from Marseille, to feature in domestic cup competitions, and was happy with that.

Gianluigi Donnarumma had a night to forget in Leipzig this week, making at least three individual errors

But Man City boss Enzo Maresca will stand by his goalkeeper, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’

Happy in a way that James Trafford was not, after making it clear that one season as Donnarumma’s understudy was not palatable.

He has flourished at Leeds United so far this season, leading to some observers criticising Hugo Viana for letting him go, only to blunder for a goal at Bournemouth last weekend. Worth remembering that it does happen to all of them at some point.

Trafford did not appear ready for the big time last year when starting the season ahead of the wantaway Ederson and City had their eyes on Donnarumma months before landing him – a £26million deal struck just as Ederson left for Fenerbahce.

Trafford will be ready soon and is pushing Jordan Pickford hard to be England's No1, but definitely wasn’t back then.

With Trafford gone and Maresca seemingly ruling out his No2 taking over – while also making a vague reference to taking stock over the international break – it appears that City would have no option but to stick with Donnarumma if they did actually want to bring about a change. January signings seem remote in the current climate of guilty verdicts and appeals.

But there is something outstanding that Donnarumma does offer, one that does set him apart. Maresca categorised the stunning one-handed save from Leipzig’s Christoph Baumgartner as one nobody else could make.

And while some hyperbole might be at play there, very few could lay claim to producing that kind of moment on a semi-regular basis.

Repelling Baumgartner is up there with Donnarumma’s instinctive save from Bryan Mbeumo at a crucial juncture on debut last year and thwarting Alexis Mac Allister in a victory at Anfield. The sort of awe-inspiring saves thousands pay money to witness.

Very few goalkeepers can claim to make wonder-saves as regularly as Donnarumma does

Donnarumma's impressive shot-stopping in the Premier League is evidenced by this graphic of every shot he has faced since joining City (red circles = goals, blank circles = saves)

Nobody across the Premier League has a higher save percentage than Donnarumma’s 71.5 since his arrival from PSG. More scientifically, only Bart Verbruggen and Senne Lammens have prevented more goals in that time – a metric measured by the xG of shots compared to how many goals were conceded.

Donnarumma has prevented seven goals (1.4 this season), with Brighton’s Verbruggen at 9.7 and Manchester United's Lammens at 8.1 across the same period. These are broadly encouraging numbers for City, despite Donnarumma's save percentage dipping to 69.7 this season – eighth among his peers, with Trafford way out in front on 79.5.

City will need to keep a careful eye on that downward trend from a 27-year-old who they brought to the club to act as the anchor, to bail them out in a way that Ederson struggled. That was the trade-off for his limited footwork, being incapable of playing through the opposition lines in a way the Brazilian could.

The wonder saves cancel all of that out. Donnarumma has been the goalkeeper’s goalkeeper for those alone. But were the certainty around that aspect of his game to waver on a longer-term basis, City should have decisions to make.

#1285. In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1,2,3,4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5,6,7,8,9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1–SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

All data generated or analysed in this study are included in this article, its Supplementary Information, source data files and Supplementary Datasets, or are available through public repositories. Raw and processed high-throughput sequencing data generated in this study, including CRISPR screen sequencing, targeted amplicon sequencing, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, CUT&RUN and WGS data, have been deposited in the Gene Expression Omnibus under the accession numbers GSE272887 and GSE335215, and the Sequence Read Archive under the accession number PRJNA1477126. Source data and statistical information for non-high-throughput experiments, including flow cytometry, protein analyses, imaging analyses and other molecular or cellular assays, are provided with this paper as source data files. Processed results and relevant quantifications from high-throughput experiments are provided in the Supplementary Datasets. The following publicly available reference datasets and resources were used in this study: the human reference genome GRCh38 Gencode v44 for bulk RNA-seq analyses; the human reference genome GRCh38 Gencode v37 for single-cell RNA-seq analyses; the human reference genome GRCh38 Gencode v47 and ENCODE blacklist regions for GRCh38 for WGS analyses; the Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB v7.4); and the ProjecTILs single-cell T cell atlas dataset. Parental cell lines are available from the commercial sources listed in the Methods and Supplementary Information. Engineered cell lines, plasmids and other research materials generated in this study are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request and completion of any required material transfer agreements. Source data are provided with this paper.

Custom code used for data analysis and figure generation in this study is available at GitHub (https://github.com/Prenauer/DKO-CAR-T).

a, Quantification of CD3− cells 5 days after CRISPR-mediated gene editing in three independent donors. b, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing with the indicated Cas9 mRNA concentrations, n = 3 biologically independent replicates. Data are shown as mean + s.e.m. Significance was calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test. ns, not significant. c, Left, representative flow cytometry plots showing CD3 and CD28 protein-level DKO efficiency in activated human primary T cells 5 days after Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Right, quantification of CD3+ CD28+ cells in DKO and vector control groups; data are shown as mean + s.e.m.; n = 4 infection replicates. Significance was calculated using a paired two-sided t-test, ****P < 0.0001. d, Quantification of CD3− or CD28− cells 5 days after editing; n = 3 donors per concentration. Data are shown as mean ± s.e.m. e, Classification and composition of targeted genes in the T cell DKO CRISPR library. f, Schematic of the two-step T cell DKO CRISPR library construction process. g, Quantification of plasmid library sgRNA-pair construct distribution. h, Flow cytometry histograms showing EGFRvIII expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. i, Flow cytometry histograms showing PD-L1 expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. j, Schematic of DKO CAR-T cell library generation pipeline, including human T cell isolation and activation, CAR-T cell generation and selection, lentiviral DKO CRISPR library infection and Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Schematic in panel j created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/4g9xapi (2026). k, Spider plots of tumour volumes for donor 1 in vivo screen experiment shown in Fig. 1d. n = 5 biologically independent mice. l, Representative H&E-stained tumour sections from two biologically independent tumours per group from the screen shown in Fig. 1c. Scale bar, 250 μm. m, sgRNA-pair detection rates from the total library across individual samples. D, donor; T, tumour. n, Heat map of Spearman correlation coefficients between the log2-normalized counts-per-million (log-norm.) sgRNA counts for each sample. Data were arranged by hierarchical clustering using the ward.D2 method. o, Multidimensional scaling analysis of log2-normalized screen data using the top 10,000 most variable sgRNA pairs across samples. Data points were clustered by k-means. p, Box-dot plot of library representation across individual samples, showing the distribution of all sgRNA-pair constructs counts. Boxes indicate the 25th–75th percentiles, center lines indicate medians, and whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5 times the interquartile range. Individual points represent sgRNA-pair counts. q, Empirical cumulative distribution function of DKO library representation among detected sgRNA pairs in plasmid, pre-injection cell and tumour samples. Sample labels in m-p indicate sample type, plasmid, pre-injection cell or tumour, and donor ID.

a, Distribution of the top four performing sgRNA-pair constructs for top DKO hits across samples, ranked by SAMBA sgRNA z-score. b, Heat map of DKO screen scores for all pairwise gene combinations assessed in the CRISPR screen. Values were scaled and visualized within a range of −1 to 1. Hierarchical clustering was performed using the Ward.D2 method based on Euclidean distances. c, Scatter plot showing the relationship between screen enrichment and synergistic effect. SAMBA z-scores were plotted against synergy scores for each gene pair. Dashed lines indicate FDR-adjusted P value, q < 0.05, for epistasis and SAMBA results. d, Scatter plot of observed DKO SAMBA scores versus expected SAMBA scores based on the additive effects of the corresponding SKOs for each gene pair (SKO1 + SKO2). Points are colored by synergy score. Linear regression yielded R2 = 0.0152 (n = 2,485 gene pairs; 71 SKO genes), indicating minimal predictability of DKO outcomes from SKO additivity. e, Quantification of indel frequencies in DKO-edited CAR-T cells 5 days after electroporation across three independent batches. P values were calculated using unpaired two-sided t-tests. Data are mean ± s.e.m.; n = 3 human donors. Each dot represents one human donor. f, Quantification of indel frequencies in CAR-T cells from three donors generated across three independent batches 90 days after gene editing. P values were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC. Data are mean + s.e.m.; n = 3 independent donor-derived CAR-T cell preparations, generated from three donors in independent batches. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing in different DKO CAR-T cells compared with controls, n = 3 infection replicates per group. b, Schematic of generation of DKO CAR-T or CAR-Jurkat cell generation and downstream assays. #1284. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

🗣️ Commitment. Resilience. Teamwork. Michael's powerful message in full 👇 https://t.co/vWwJt1fW47

This was partly Carrick reasserting his own authority after a couple of weeks in which two senior players – defender Lisandro Martínez and captain Bruno Fernandes – decided to go public with their grievances and the team delivered a performance in the 4-1 hammering by Como that was up there with the very worst.

But a stony-faced Carrick was also sending a message to his squad to quit their public sniping and start pulling together for a wider cause. Moreover, to put the club and the team before yourself and your individual needs and complaints.

It was interesting that he used the word “entitlement”. His predecessor, Ruben Amorim, had uttered that same word to attack what he felt was an “entitlement culture” at the club and Carrick has evidently come to a similar conclusion.

#1283. Spalletti: ‘Juventus must build on positive signs, otherwise back to square one’

Luciano Spalletti insists Juventus ‘showed positive signs’ when beating Napoli, but they must build on those in the Europa League with AZ Alkmaar ‘otherwise we go back to square one.’

It kicks off in Alkmaar at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens on the Liveblog.

The Bianconeri got back on track domestically with their 2-0 victory against Napoli on Sunday, and are unbeaten so far in the Europa League with two wins and a 2-2 draw with Stade Rennais.

However, injuries rule out Weston McKennie, Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Nico Gonzalez, Francisco Conceicao, Zeki Celik, Khephren Thuram and Kamil Grabara.

“Alajbegovic works well with the rest of the team, he can pass the ball and cut inside, creating a moment out of nowhere to shock the opposition, as we saw against Napoli,” Spalletti told Sky Sport Italia.

“There is also an opportunity for us to rotate ahead of the trip to Fiorentina. We changed four this evening, but what becomes fundamental is to repeat the kind of performance we saw with Napoli.

“That match showed clear signals, it is important to recognise their power and repeat them with more emphasis and consistency in future, otherwise we go straight back to square one. From here on is the opportunity for real growth.”

McKennie is left out due to a fitness issue, although he should be back this weekend in Serie A, so Pape Matar Sarr steps into the starting XI.

“McKennie is someone who knows how to encapsulate the mentality of a strong team, he fights everywhere all over the pitch to help out, he is convinced of his own strength,” explained Spalletti.

“Pape Sarr plays this evening and we want to see how he can repeat what he did at Tottenham in important matches. I want the best out of my players, just like we did in the last game.

“We’ve got Juan Cabal and Lloyd Kelly back to fitness, we trust these lads, but they too need to prove they’ve got the right attitude.”

AZ Alkmaar are unbeaten at home in 17 UEFA matches going back to October 2023, so are a tough prospect here.

“They haven’t lost here in a long time, so we need a great performance,” warned Spalletti.

“We can’t come here and think of controlling the match, we need to raise the level, recognise the importance of the gestures made during the game, and repeat them more consistently, even constantly.

“I did see positive signs from the team, and it is essential we repeat them tonight. AZ Alkmaar have a clear identity, they know what they want to do, they all know what they need to play there. Juventus still need to fully understand that.”

#1282. Can Portugal Retire Cristiano Ronaldo’s No.7 Shirt

Many wondered if this news would ever come, but yes, Cristiano Ronaldo has finally retired from international football. Now 41, the veteran forward has played his final game for Portugal.

The Al-Nassr star bows out with 146 goals in 234 caps for his country, having also won Euro 2016. In his departing message, he said: "To the Portuguese people, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and taking it with me to stadiums all over the world. Today the moment has come to hand it over to the future. It wasn't an easy decision, because there are decisions that aren't made only with the head. They are also made with the heart."

For club and country, the number seven shirt has become synonymous with Ronaldo. As such, despite his claims that it's 'time to return the jersey,' some are wondering if Portugal will instead retire the number as an acknowledgement of his special career.

However, it might not be quite so simple as just making one decision.

The 41-year-old has retired from international football, havign scored a record 146 goals in 234 Portugal caps.

A little-known FIFA rule stops international shirt numbers from being retired. Ronaldo actually started out wearing No.16 when he made his debut in 2003, but was handed the No.7 shirt in 2008. He wore it as he lifted Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles, while also becoming the all-time men’s international top goalscorer.

Had he achieved that level of success at a club team, maybe he would have seen the shirt number retired. Johan Cruyff (14 at Ajax), Paolo Maldini (3 at AC Milan), and Franco Baresi (6 also at Milan) are all among the legendary footballers to have had their shirt numbers retired, while Liverpool paid respect to Diogo Jota by retiring his No.20 jersey after his tragic passing in 2025.

Ronaldo, though, will have to pass on the number seven shirt to another Portuguese star. This is because national teams are required to designate consecutive numbers for every player in the squad for FIFA and FIFA confederation tournaments. At the 2026 World Cup, for example, sides were made up of 26 players, meaning squad numbers had to go from 1 to 26. As such, it would be a breach of rules to skip past the number seven on a tournament-going squad list.

Perhaps this isn't the worst rule in the world. After all, Argentina once tried to retire the No.10 shirt in honour of World Cup-winning great Diego Maradona. They had a request denied by FIFA ahead of the 2002 World Cup, but the number was fittingly later won by Lionel Messi, who would win the 2022 World Cup and match his predecessor's legacy.

Despite also having many past greats, Portugal have never requested to retire a number before. Ballon d'Or winner Luis Figo used to wear No.7, while the likes of Nani and Ricardo Quaresma even donned it while Ronaldo was absent.

It's worth noting that when Ronaldo quit the Portugal camp early in September, Rafael Leao took on the vacant No.7 shirt for the two remaining Nations League fixtures. It remains to be seen if he will wear that number in the upcoming break later this month.

#1281. Long balls are NOT banned at Newcastle! Matthias Jaissle insists his criticism after Everton defeat was lost in translation - having said stars were failing to follow tactics

Published: 11:50 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EDT, 5 November 2026

Matthias Jaissle says his criticism of Newcastle’s players was lost in translation and has clarified that long balls are not forbidden under his management.

The head coach also believes that his squad understands what is being asked of them, although he says his door remains open to any player seeking clarity over his instructions.

In the wake of Monday’s 1-0 home defeat by Everton, Jaissle said that the players had failed to follow his instruction and bemoaned their use of long balls when the plan was to keep it on the floor.

Asked if those comments had been addressed with the squad this week, Jaissle said: ‘I don't know if it's a misinterpretation or a language barrier, but there is an element of that when I explained that in the press conference.

‘But it is indeed (something) we address, because we talked sometimes about the no-risk zone, where we had previously critical-ball losses leading to goals. Of course, if there is a clear risk for ball loss, then I prefer playing a long ball to our striker and protecting the ball and develop the game from there.

‘It (my comments) are not to point any fingers, not at all. Sometimes you are willing to do something, but on that day it just did not work and you make the wrong decisions. It comes also with confidence.

Matthias Jaissle, pictured giving instructions during Newcastle's defeat by Everton, has insisted long balls are not banned

'If you have scenarios where you can find easily your team-mate on the ground and we build up from there with our patterns, then you should for sure also prefer that.

‘But it's not easy, it's easier said from outside. If the confidence is missing, then you prefer to be really safe and shooting maybe even more the long ball.’

Daily Mail Sport was told this week that some players are ‘confused’ by exactly what it is Jaissle wants from them, but the head coach said: ‘The fundamental thing is that we can count on unity and togetherness.

'The door is always open if ever there is anything unclear. If you see the training then I’m pretty sure everyone understands and is fully committed. There was never a question, at least I’m not aware of it.

‘It’s important we listen to the players. If there is anything unclear, they will drop in.’

Meanwhile, Jaissle says he retains the support of the club’s hierarchy after a run of four defeats in five matches.

‘The nice part is that I got even more the feeling from within the club how committed they are (this week),’ he said.

‘That just shows me that everyone believes in the long-term project and that everyone is also aware and realistic about the journey and where we are right now.’

The excellent John Percy believes that Unai Emery now can claim to be the best manager in the Premier League, with few able to match his track record.

He writes: “With Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp having departed the Premier League, there can now be little doubt that Unai Emery is the best manager in England’s top division. And by some distance.

“Saturday will mark four years since Villa unveiled Emery as their head coach and few could have predicted the success that has followed. He has proved an inspired appointment who has continually embarrassed the “Big Six” clubs.

“On every level, he has delivered: points per game, net spend, a distinguishable style of play, improving individual players, over-performance in the league and European competition.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1279. Amorim: ‘No explanation for Milan performance, we are not ready to play’

Ruben Amorim was furious and bemused by Milan’s 2-0 Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros. ‘There is no explanation. We were not prepared to play football. We are not ready to play every three days.’

The Rossoneri cannot seem to find any consistency, as they can follow up the 3-1 Derby della Madonnina triumph against rivals Inter with this remarkably sluggish performance in the same stadium.

Lenny Joseph pounced on two defensive and goalkeeping errors to beat 21-year-old Lorenzo Torriani, deputising for suspended Mike Maignan and injured Pietro Terracciano, to give Ferencvaros a 2-0 victory at San Siro.

“There is no explanation. There is nothing I can say, especially about the first half,” confessed a visibly shaken Amorim to Sky Sport Italia.

“I don’t remember us playing any other first half performances like that. This is about ambition, concentration. We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight.”

How does the coach think this can be the same team that ran riot against Inter at the weekend in Serie A, yet had such a totally different approach?

“It is difficult to explain,” added Amorim.

“Quite simply, we were not ready to go from the derby to this competition. When you play with the Milan jersey, you have a responsibility, and you cannot turn up like this.

“Probably I didn’t do enough to make sure the team was ready.”

There are quite a few injuries that reduce the options, but after three defeats in the opening four Europa League matches, it is evident they struggle on a Thursday evening.

“We are not ready to be competitive on two fronts. We’ve got to work on our approach and the way we view football. There are no excuses tonight, there is nothing that I can say.

“I usually have a lot to say to defend my team, but tonight I really don’t. We must be humble and try to understand what happened.”

It is not the first time that Milan have stepped up several gears in the big games, only to crumble when they seem to take things for granted, so what can Amorim do about this situation that goes back long before his arrival?

“Perhaps I did something wrong over the last two days, but I saw the team had similar problems last season. We have to find a solution. We were not ready tonight, we showed no courage. If we don’t win, we should at least do everything we can to turn the situation around, but we didn’t see that tonight.”

It was the first match where Strahinja Pavlovic was allowed rest after playing almost every minute of the season so far, and Amorim admits the defender was missed.

“Everyone ought to train like Pavlovic. He is ready to die in training, he sets a good example. At times, players struggle when they do not start matches, but there are no excuses, we ought to have won with those who started too.

“We have to fix it! We cannot think that this is just how it goes. We should’ve done so many things better this evening,” said an increasingly agitated Amorim.

“Just being better on the second balls would’ve helped. We were just not in the game.”

At this stage, losing three of the opening four, it is likely Milan won’t be able to turn this around and stay in the Europa League beyond January.

“I have to think about Serie A, obviously, but we do need to do well in the Europa League too. We can and must win games despite squad rotation. We have to be ready, and right now we are not, to play and win every three days.

“I will not give up on this competition, though, so as long as it is mathematically possible, we will fight in this competition just like the others.”

#1278. Liverpool Confidential: Billionaires' investment set to beat deadline, new deal for Trey Nyoni, the academy kids who shone in Istanbul and Mor Talla Ndiaye's visa issues

Published: 12:00 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EDT, 5 November 2026

The deal for a group of billionaires to buy a minority stake in Liverpool remains on track to pass a deadline set by the new independent football regulator.

The consortium led by Amit Bhatia, known as 1892 Holdings, agreed to purchase a 38 per cent stake in Fenway Sports Group’s controlling interest in the club earlier this season. And despite some anxieties externally and in the fanbase about a lack of updates, I have been told this week that everything is moving in the right direction.

Sources close to Bhatia and his consortium insist the process takes time but there are no hitches and it is still expected to beat the deadline. It is understood the date in question is in December and in accordance with the new regulator, who must take within 90 days to issue a final suitability determination for prospective new owners or senior executives.

Indeed, this week brought the news that FSG are in exploratory talks to buy a significant stake in Formula One team Cadillac. Both FSG and Cadillac were contacted for comment around that story – and insisted it is an ongoing process.

One source pointed to the fact that FSG clearly expect to have some ‘spare pennies lying around’ – hinting the Liverpool investment will go through.

Senior FSG staff have constantly stressed that selling 38 per cent of the club does not mean they are losing interest and that they are as committed as ever, though the potential for the buy-in to become a full-scale takeover at some point in the future remains.

Bhatia is backed by his billionaire father-in-law Lakshmi Mittal, plus Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin.

Amit Bhatia (second left) is heading up a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool from John Henry (second right) and his Fenway Sports Group

Liverpool supporters hope the deal will transform the club's fortunes on the pitch

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool – and Andoni Iraola ruled him out for more than a month with a problem he suffered at Brentford on October 17.

I understand the Dutch international is now all-but fit and could play this weekend if needed – however, given his high number of injuries, a decision has been made to delay his return.

Liverpool were recently punished for bringing back Dominik Szoboszlai too quickly as the Hungarian pulled up shortly after his first start upon his return, which set him back a fortnight.

Frimpong missed only seven Bayer Leverkusen games through injury in four years at the club according to Transfermarkt, but has already sat out nearly 30 Liverpool matches. Most of those absences have been hamstring related, so Frimpong is not being rushed back and will be given the international break to continue working on his recovery.

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool and went down again against Brentford last month. However, the Dutch international is now close to a return

Trey Nyoni has been offered a bumper new contract to reward him for his fine progress.

The 19-year-old, who scored his first Liverpool goal in the defeat in Istanbul against Fenerbahce on Wednesday night, has had a stellar rise since Iraola took over at Liverpool.

Nyoni, signed from Leicester City in 2023, was in many matchday squads and featured sparingly last season but has come of age this campaign and has already doubled his first-team minutes – with three quarters of the season still to play.

Nottingham Forest made a £30million bid in the summer but Iraola identified him as a key asset and he will be rewarded handsomely for his progress.

Trey Nyoni scored his first Liverpool goal on Wednesday night in the Champions League loss against Fenerbahce

Your question answered: What's the January priority?

One topic fans have asked me about this week is which position is a priority in the January and summer transfer windows.

The first area to mention is midfield. I have reported in the past how Chelsea are currently ahead of Liverpool in the race for Bournemouth's Alex Scott, so let’s keep an eye on that – and the situation of Lamine Camara of Monaco. But I think the priority has to be a left-back.

Are Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas good enough? Neither have performed at the required level so far this season and bringing Tsimikas back from a loan at Roma – where he barely played – felt like a bit of a cop-out. It has to be a priority position in the next 12 months.

Liverpool flew straight home from Istanbul after the loss to Fenerbahce and did not land on Merseyside until past 2am. It is a departure from last season, when Arne Slot would often have his squad stay for two nights on European away days.

Players are said to be big fans of the extra night at home with most preferring to sleep in their own beds.

Iraola did not hold a post-match team talk after Fenerbahce but will debrief the squad when back in training, having branded the defeat ‘cheap’ and ‘messy’.

Another UEFA Youth League game, another hat-trick for Will Wright.

I was in place on the outskirts of Istanbul on Wednesday afternoon to watch the 18-year-old bag his second treble in four European matches this term, making it 13 goals for the season in all competitions.

Wright had a heated exchange with Josh Sonni-Lambie over who would take a penalty but the pair have smoothed things over now after Wright took it and scored. The striker’s assist for Finn Inglethorpe was also a notable moment that showed he is a team player and not a greedy No9.

Liverpool's Will Wright scored another hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday, against Fenerbahce Under 19s

I was also impressed by right back Oliver O’Connor, who looks like a real athlete. He aced every physical pre-season test for the academy and is versatile, with a quality delivery into the penalty area.

The Scouser joined the club aged six and has been a midfielder for most of his career. Boss Rob Page does not necessarily see him as a right back long-term but he caught the eye up and down that flank.

Those who did watch the academy game – and the first-team later on – would have been wondering where defender Mor Talla Ndiaye was. He is a mainstay in the Youth League XI and has been on the seniors’ bench several times.

It is believed the Senegalese defender had a visa issue and could not feature in the game in Turkey, though next month’s away match in Bruges is not expected to pose the same problem.

Liverpool's Mor Talla Ndiaye (centre) was nowhere to be seen in Istanbul due to visa issues

Also in academy news, young midfielder Michael Laffey has signed with the OmniSports agency who represent the likes of Wright and Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. Under 21s captain Laffey, whose dad owns the Glenbuck pub in Anfield, made the first-team bench a fortnight ago.

Liverpool supporters have drawn the short straw and will pay more than any of their English counterparts for a pint while following their team in Europe this season.

That’s according to data from LiveScore, who have worked out that Reds will pay an average of £4.91 per pint on their travels.

Still, £4.91 for a pint? Better than most places at home. You might need one after watching Liverpool’s defending this week!

#1277. Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 49–57 (2026) Cite this article

The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III–V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

#1276. Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has quickly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

Treatment is needed for Zubimendi after he is caught on the nose by Barry.

Big chance for Everton. Garner whips a teasing cross into the box, Dewsbury-Hall meets it with his head on the run but the ball flies just wide of the post.

EvertonOFF Johnson, Mykolenko ON Dibling, Hackney

Tarkowski is the latest yellow card for Everton after a foul on Havertz.

Eze with a poor cross into the box. He fails to run back quickly and Arteta sprints to the edge of the touchline and goes berserk at the midfielder.

How have Arsenal reacted to their top scorer Saka being injured? Both of their centre backs have scored for the first time this season.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

It is a lovely move with slick one-touch passing. The ball is fed to White making a run down the outside and he clips the ball to the far post for Gabriel to head home.

OFF Merino, Lewis-Skelly, GyokeresON Calafiori, Guimaraes, Havertz

Garner is booked for Everton now after barging into Merino off the ball.

Arteta is shown a yellow card for something. Not sure what for yet. But the Arsenal manager is looking to make some changes off the bench.

Arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

Arsenal have defensive options in Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori and Mosquera if Arteta wants to avoid taking any risks.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Gabriel immediately raised his hand for medical attention after making that clearance. He really extended his leg to get the ball away. Looks to be in a lot of pain.

Latest corner from Arsenal after Eze’s shot is blocked by Rohl. Rice’s delivery into the near post is headed clear to Odegaard, who shoots ambitiously from distance and Pickford collects the ball comfortably.

Arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!

Big chance for Everton. White thinks he has time when he heads the ball back to Raya but he does not connect well and Barry is there to pick it up and he flicks a shot at goal but Raya reacts quickly to parry the ball.

Raya is penalised for taking too long with the ball and Everton have a cheap corner. Danger is cleared by Arsenal as they force Everton back into their half.

The conditions are terrible at the moment. Heavy wind and rain causing havoc.

A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

Madueke should do better. Rice finds him and the winger drives into the box. He takes a shot but drags a right-footed effort wide.

Chance for Arsenal. Rice finds space behind the Everton midfield and drives forward. He plays a pass to Lewis-Skelly, who lays it off to Eze. The England midfielder sidefoots a cross into the box but no one in an Arsenal shirt is there to meet it.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

George is looking lively for Everton. He tries to come inside and whip an effort to the far corner but the ball deflects wide.

From the corner, Gabriel clears off the line after Raya loses track of the ball.

Everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

Everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any plans to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.
